rationale: C10 supplies the closest concrete drafting model: a statute assigns an initial technical determination to a cabinet secretary following public process and then calls for a presidential proclamation giving formal effect to that determination. The child uses substantially the same two-stage machinery, with the Secretary of the Interior adopting regulations after notice and public procedure and submitting them to the President, who then approves and proclaims them. The subjects and underlying statutes differ, and the shared ceremonial proclamation language is boilerplate, but the secretary-to-President decisional sequence is material enough to make reuse plausible. C06 is weaker because it also promulgates extensive codified regulations but lacks the same prior-secretarial-action-and-presidential-approval sequence. C03 shares wildlife subject matter and regulatory authority but not the child's machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Secretary of the Interior has adopted, after notice and public procedure ... and has submitted to me for approval the following amendments
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Secretary of the Treasury, after due notice and opportunity for public hearing, has found the drug Isoamidone ...
shared_material.explanation: Both predicates rest on a cabinet secretary completing a statutorily contemplated technical action after public process.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby approve and proclaim the foregoing amendments
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby proclaim that the Secretary of the Treasury has found the drug Isoamidone ...
shared_material.explanation: Both proclamations use presidential action to formally validate or give effect to the secretary's preceding determination.
